newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE March coffee futures end up almost six pct.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE March coffee futures end up almost six pct.

text.p: LIFFE robusta futures rose almost six percent to end Wednesday at $1,545 a tonne basis March and just below a high of $1,550 on fund buying triggered by Colombian export news.
"The Colombian news was the fuse that light the fireworks," said one trader.
"The fund buying in London and New York pushed it up as well," he added.
By the close, benchmark March contract was 5.6 percent or $82 at $1,545 a tonne. The position was also six percent up on the day on Tuesday on news of lower Brazilian crop forecasts.
"The market is stretching itself up again and again. We are not sure how long and how far the funds want to push it now," a trader said.
A senior Colombian official said in Rio de Janeiro that the country's coffee exports in January could be 300,000 bags less than less anticipated if a continuing strike at its main port continued.
Early Wednesday, talks aimed at ending a week-long dockworkers' strike ended in a stalemate.
New York arabica futures surged to new contract highs by midsession as traders continued to fret about near-term supply.
London prices spent the morning flat to slightly down on trade profit-taking.
Traders said the March's close at a comfortable $1,545 level could provide an impetus for an assault towards the next hurdle at $1,615-$1,620 region.
The market's ascent was again met with little or no origin selling.

The Association of Producing Countries (ACPC) council meets in Rio de Janeiro on Thursday to consider an African proposal calling for an export cut of 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997 to lock in higher prices.
The meeting will be preceded by an ACPC technical meeting on Wednesday.
An African plan envisaged a reduction of 1.5 million tonnes in arabica exports and the remaining one million in robusta. But some traders thought any cutbacks would be weighted towards robusta.

"I don't think anyone believes the entire cut will be robustas but we will wait and see what happens on Friday," the trader said. He added in view of the time difference, any major ACPC impact would only be felt in the London market on Friday.
But others felt that with the recent rises in arabica and robusta prices, there would be less pressure for producers to undertake a drastic cut.
Volume reached a sizeable 13,275 lots. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 5424985
